title: NY State Senate · District 33
area: Central and south Bronx, including Kingsbridge Heights, Tremont, East Tremont, Crotona, Fordham, Belmont, Van Nest, and Morris Park.

context.text: Both the Democratic and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled; incumbent J. Gustavo Rivera advanced on both lines without appearing on a primary ballot. As of this writing, no Republican or other opposition candidate has filed for the general election, leaving Rivera unopposed on the ballot.

candidates.name: J. Gustavo Rivera
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed; no Republican or third-party opponent has filed for the general election.

priorities.text: Healthcare expansion, including sponsorship of the New York Health Act to create a state single-payer health plan.
Reducing medical debt for New Yorkers.
Substance-use treatment and harm reduction, including through the Opioid Settlement Fund and a Safer Consumption Services Act.
Safe-staffing standards in hospitals and nursing homes.
Advocacy for Latino communities in the Bronx.

positions.summary: Sponsors the New York Health Act, which would create a state single-payer health plan, and sponsored S9589, which would create a state-funded premium-assistance program and expand Essential Plan eligibility for New Yorkers losing coverage due to federal policy changes under H.R. 1.

record.text: Sponsored S9573, authorizing the state Health Commissioner to establish regional Medicaid waiting lists for the Nursing Home Transition and Diversion waiver program once federally approved capacity is reached; passed the Senate 61–0 on June 2, 2026 and passed the Assembly by June 4, 2026.

Sponsored S9401-A, directing the Health Department to enable data exchange between the state's Prescription Monitoring Program registry and certified electronic health record systems; passed the Senate 60–0 on May 13, 2026 (via substitute A8849) and returned to the Assembly.

Sponsored S9589, which would create a state-funded premium-assistance program and expand Essential Plan eligibility for New Yorkers losing insurance coverage because of the federal H.R. 1 reconciliation law; in Senate Health Committee as of March 26, 2026.

Chairs the Senate Health Committee in the 2025–2026 session and also sits on the Alcoholism and Substance Abuse, Housing, Mental Health, Crime Victims Crime and Correction, Finance, and Higher Education committees.
